svg.title: Flower Anatomy Drag & Drop
svg.desc: A static, script-free SVG labeling activity. Select word-bank tiles to pick them up, follow numbered leader arrows to the parts of a flower, and open Hint, Check Answer and Reset panels. All interaction is done with internal anchor links and the CSS :target selector; there is no JavaScript and no external asset.

g.text: Plant reproduction, lesson 4. Label the ten parts of a flowering plant.

svg.text: Not to scale. The near petals are cut away to show the reproductive organs inside.

g.text: Label the flower in four steps
Select any label in the word bank below. It lifts
and turns green while you are holding it.
Each numbered slot points to one flower part.
A dashed outline means a whole structure.
Place all ten labels; each one is used once.
The part spotlight explains the tile you hold.
Stuck? Open Hint. Finished? Check Answer shows
the key. Reset clears the board to start again.
Pick up a tile to read what that part does.
A tube grows down the style
Ovule to seed, ovary to fruit
Pick up a label, then drop it on a numbered slot.
Each tile has a grip handle. Selecting one picks it up; selecting another swaps it.
The sticky tip of the pistil. It catches and holds
pollen grains brought by wind or animals.
Now choose the numbered slot where this label belongs.
Green, leaf-like parts on the outside that protect
the flower bud before it opens.
Now choose the numbered slot where this label belongs.
The thin stalk of the stamen. It holds the anther
up where pollinators can brush against it.
Now choose the numbered slot where this label belongs.
The thickened top of the flower stalk. Every other
floral part, from sepals to pistil, is attached here.
Now choose the numbered slot where this label belongs.
Brightly coloured, often scented parts that attract
pollinators. Together the petals form the corolla.
Now choose the numbered slot where this label belongs.
The swollen base of the pistil that holds the ovules.
After fertilisation it develops into the fruit.
Now choose the numbered slot where this label belongs.
The sac at the top of the stamen where pollen
grains are made and then released.
Now choose the numbered slot where this label belongs.
The female organ of the flower (also called the
carpel). It is made of the stigma, style and ovary.
Now choose the numbered slot where this label belongs.
The slender stalk joining stigma to ovary. Pollen
tubes grow down through it to reach the ovules.
Now choose the numbered slot where this label belongs.
The male organ of the flower. Each stamen is an
anther held up on a filament, and it makes pollen.
Now choose the numbered slot where this label belongs.
Holding a tile: choose a numbered slot
The answer key is on the diagram
Compare each green slot with where you placed your labels, then close the key to keep working.
Give yourself one point for each label that matches.
5 to 7: read the hints. 0 to 4: reset and try again.
The four rings of a flower, seen from above
Sepals form the outer green ring; petals sit just inside them.
The pollen sac sits on top; the thin stalk below holds it up.
Read it top to bottom: sticky tip, slender tube, swollen base.
Dashed outlines wrap a whole organ
Slots 7 and 8 point to complete structures, not single parts.
The receptacle is the swollen tip of the stalk that holds it all.
Still stuck? Pick up any tile and read its definition in the part spotlight.
Every placed label goes back to the word bank
and all ten slots are cleared.
How pollination leads to seeds and fruit
Anthers split open and release thousands of grains.
A bee, bird or the wind carries it to a stigma.
The grain grows a tube down the style to an ovule.
The ovule becomes a seed; the ovary becomes fruit.
Board reset. All ten tiles are back in the word bank.
